title: HSIZE Alignment and Natural Byte Lanes
description: Little-endian examples on a 32-bit bus pair each address/size with the previous transfer's active write-data lanes and flag a misaligned halfword.

annotations.message: Address phase: a BYTE at 0x00 is aligned. Its payload will use HWDATA[7:0] in the following data phase.
Data 0xA5 for address 0x00 appears on lane [7:0], while a new BYTE address 0x01 is accepted for lane [15:8].
The byte for 0x01 is shifted onto HWDATA[15:8]. The simultaneous HALFWORD address 0x02 is aligned and will use lanes [31:16].
The halfword for 0x02 occupies HWDATA[31:16]. The simultaneous WORD at 0x04 is aligned and will use all four byte lanes.
The word for 0x04 uses HWDATA[31:0]. The new HALFWORD address 0x01 is illegal because address bit 0 is set.

A legal-traffic generator must not emit the misaligned transfer. In an intentional negative test, the monitor reports it and the implementation's downstream response/recovery is checked only against the documented design policy; AHB defines no synthetic BLOCK data phase.

violations.message: Halfword transfer at 0x01 is not aligned to a two-byte boundary.
